user_question: Whether the proposed 40-second test is really the ideal choice.

decision.scope: First technical native delivery test and reusable planned opening sample.

why_keep_40_seconds: The range exactly matches an existing registered opening, rather than creating a disposable new comparison window. If delivery succeeds with native provenance, retain the same bytes for the later opening review.

It is bounded enough for a first file-transfer/decode test and gives opening context beyond a single image or a short codec header. It can expose actual frame content and audible source material, if present.
Shortening the range offers no demonstrated provider-unit saving: published pricing is by format/job with a long-source multiplier. Units and transfer savings remain unmeasured.

Downloading the full 3h31m48s source before proving delivery would expand transfer/storage exposure; the bounded requested output is preferable for this first access check, without claiming bounded source ingestion.

first_test_acceptance.received_media: Receive actual media bytes, preserve provider job/request/delivery lineage and SHA256; metadata, tool list, thumbnails and player-ready messages do not satisfy this.
first_test_acceptance.decode: Probe and decode the complete returned clip, both video and audio streams. Record actual dimensions, frame timing/count, audio timing and decode errors; a request parameter alone does not prove 1080p or exact trim.
first_test_acceptance.perceptual_review: Inspect native images and listen to decoded source audio with timestamps; document what the opening actually contains. A static image, initial fade or silence is not automatically an acquisition failure or a semantic quality pass.
first_test_acceptance.source_mapping: Retain exact requested and returned source-clock information; explain offsets/duration differences instead of accepting filename or local timestamp zero as source identity.
first_test_acceptance.resource_measurement: Observe actual provider units, transfer bytes, latency/runtime and storage, with zero-additional-spend stop conditions before any request. No paid upgrade, card or recharge.
first_test_acceptance.result_scope: A successful access test closes only native delivery for this one opening. It does not approve the full reference, other sources, complete release or recurring throughput.
first_test_acceptance.reuse: If successful, preserve this asset and evidence; do not download the same opening again to start the later review.

what_remains_after_success: Review the other already registered windows/sources one at a time, reusing prior approved evidence and respecting the existing exclusion of contradictory model-only audio claims.
Measure repeated source access and the planned workload against actual unit, bandwidth, runtime and storage limits before considering a permanent recurring dependency.
Complete native market semantic handoff, then complete release qualification under final review v3. Keep production/publication/supervisor OFF until their existing gates pass.
